Though these appeals are listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties,
they are taken up for final disposal..
2.

These appeals are arising out of the judgment and award dated 18.04.2016 passed in MVC No.719/2013 on the file of MACT-XII, Ballari (for short, 'Tribunal')
3. MFA No.103048/2016 is filed by Insurance Company (i.e.United India Insurance Company Ltd.)
challenging liability as well as quantum of compensation and MFA No.102941/2016 is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation.

4. Brief facts leading to filing these appeals are that the husband of claimant No.1 Sri.Ravindra @
Ravi Kumar who was working as a cleaner in lorry bearing registration No.KA-35/4287 was proceedings in the said lorry on 20.01.2013, at that time, the driver of the lorry in rash and negligent manner dashed to the stationed NC: 2024:KHC-D:11439 lorry bearing registration No.KA-02/D-2795 which resulted in sustaining grievous injuries to the said Ravindra and later he succumbed to the injuries.
The Jurisdictional Police registered the crime, investigated and filed chargesheet against the driver of the offending lorry bearing registration No.KA-35/4287.
Wife and other legal representatives of the deceased Ravindra filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the accidental death of Sri.Ravindra.
5. Respondents entered appearance before the Tribunal and opposed the claim petition by denying liability, age, income and avocation of the deceased and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. The Tribunal recorded the evidence of the parties.

Claimant No.1 examined herself as PW1,
another witness as PW2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P15.
The respondents examined RW1, RW2 and got marked Exs.R1 to R3.

The Tribunal on appreciation of evidence available NC:
2024:KHC-D:11439 on record awarded total compensation of Rs.10,44,500/- along with interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of petition till realization by saddling the liability on the Insurance Company (i.e.United India Insurance Co., Ltd.) Being aggrieved by the same, these appeals have been filed.
7.

Sri. N.R.Kuppelur, learned counsel appearing for appellant-Insurance Company (i.e.United India Insurance Company Limited) submits that the Tribunal has committed error in saddling the entire liability on the appellant-Insurance Company without appreciating the fact that the driver of stationed lorry i.e. bearing registration No.KA-02/D-2795 was parked on the middle of the road without taking any precaution, hence, he seeks to saddle 50% of the liability on another lorry.

He further submits that the Tribunal has awarded higher compensation on all other heads, hence, the Smt.Madhavi vs Ramaiah S/O Yanadhi on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34584651/
5 question of considering the appeal for enhancement of compensation would not arise.

Further, he submits that the Tribunal has NC: 2024:KHC-D:11439 committed error in awarding interest at the rate of 7% per annum on the compensation amount which is required to be reduced to 6% per annum.
He further submits that the driver of the offending lorry was not possessing a valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident, hence insurer is not liable to pay compensation.
Thus, he seeks for allowing the appeal filed by the Insurance Company.

8. Sri.S.K.Kayakamath, learned counsel appearing for Sriram General Insurance Company Limited submits that the Tribunal taking note of the evidence available on record, more particularly the chargesheet material, has come to the conclusion that the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.KA-35/4287 was negligent, hence, the question of saddling liability on Sriram General Insurance Company Limited (i.e.insurer of lorry bearing registration No.KA-02/D-2795) would not arise.
Thus, he seeks for dismissal of both the appeals.

Sri.G.R.Turamari, learned counsel appearing for the claimants submits that the Tribunal has committed grave error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/- per month without appreciating the fact that the deceased was working as a cleaner and further submits that the Tribunal has also committed error in awarding 30% compensation under the head of future prospects of the deceased which is contrary to the principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others1.

sentences.text: Further, he also submits that the award of compensation by the Tribunal on all other heads is also on lower side which is to be modified.
Thus, he seeks to allow the appeal filed by the appellants- claimants.
10. I have heard the arguments of the learned counsel appearing for the parties and meticulously perused the material available on record.
It is not in dispute that in a road traffic accident dated 20.01.2013, the husband of claimant No.1 Sri.Ravindra @ Ravi Kumar sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The Jurisdictional Police registered the said accident as crime and took up the investigation, after completion of investigation, have filed chargesheet against the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.KA-35/4287.
The chargesheet material indicates that the driver of the said offending lorry was negligent.
In order to disprove the contents of the chargesheet, the appellant-Insurance Company (i.e.United India Insurance Company Ltd.) has not adduced any evidence before the Tribunal.
In my considered view, the Tribunal is justified in saddling the entire liability on the United India Insurance Company Ltd.
The saddling of liability by the Tribunal is strictly inconsonance of the evidence available on record and does not call for any modification.

- 11 - Smt.Madhavi vs Ramaiah S/O Yanadhi on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34584651/
6 NC: 2024:KHC-D:11439 12.

Insofar as the contention of the insurer that the driver of the offending lorry bearing registration No.KA- 35/4287 was not possessing valid and effective driving licence on the date of accident is taken note for the purpose of rejection only.
Admittedly, the insurance company had not made any attempt to find out whether the driver of the offending lorry was having valid and effective driving licence on the date of the accident.
The chargesheet material indicates that the Police have not filed the chargesheet under Section 3 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the driver of the offending lorry.

In the absence of invoking Section 3 of the MV Act by the Police in the chargesheet, I am of the considered view that the contention urged by the appellant-Insurance Company does not hold the merit, accordingly, the same is rejected.

13. Insofar as the entitlement of compensation is concerned, admittedly the claimants have not placed any cogent, legal or acceptable evidence on record before the - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11439 Tribunal with regard to the income of the deceased.
Hence, this Court re-assesses the income of the deceased notionally at Rs.7,000/- per month by placing reliance on the notional income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

Keeping in mind the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), the claimants are entitled to addition of 40% towards the assessed income of the deceased under the head of loss of future prospects.
14. There is no dispute with regard to the application of multiplier as 17 and deduction of 1/4th towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.

Thus, the appellants/claimants are entitled to modified compensation under the head of loss of dependency as under:
Rs.7,000 + 40% x 12 x 17 x  = Rs.14,99,400/-
15.

The claimants being the wife, children and parents of the deceased are entitled to Rs.44,000/-
each - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11439 under the head of loss of consortium which includes escalation at the rate of 10%.

The claimants are also entitled to Rs.16,500/- under the heads of loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- under the head of transportation of dead body and funeral expenses, which includes escalation at the rate of 10%, respectively.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled to modified compensation on the following heads:
 Particulars Amount  (in Rs.)
 Loss of dependency 14,99,400/-
 Loss of estate 16,500/-

7  Transportation of dead body and 16,500/-
 funeral expenses Loss of consortium (Rs.44,000 X 5 2,20,000/-
 dependants)
 Total 17,52,400/-
Thus, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.17,52,400/- as against Rs.10,44,500/- awarded by the Tribunal.

In the result, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER a) Both the appeals stand allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.17,52,400/- as against Rs.10,44,500/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment.
d) The Insurance Company (i.e.United India Insurance Company Ltd.) shall deposit the compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
- 15 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11439 e) Apportionment, deposit and disbursement shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.

f) Registry to transmit amount in deposit, if any, along with records, if any, to the Tribunal,
forthwith.
g) Draw modified award accordingly.
